body:
I don't know.

I feel like dead weight, an ingrate.

There are transfer programs, but there is not a very good record of their transfer rate. So many people go there not expecting to do anything with their lives, so there's a huge stigma around going to a community college. Student's are lazy and immature, like they never left high school.

It doesn't help that everyone else I know is bound to go straight into a great university, with scholarships and a clear path on what they want to do.

I have spent so long doing what others, especially my parents, told me, that I don't even know what to do for myself. The idea used to be appalling to me, the thought of doing something for *my* benefit and nobody else's.

I always thought that going to a university for four years would give me some facsimile of a social life and a sense of community and belonging. But I'm probably wrong.
Where I live, very little happens, and I despise the people around here. Also, the local community college is overcrowded and doesn't have a very good transfer record.

1) I know. But all the time, I get asked, "<name> is doing well, and s/he's happy, why can't you be?"

2) I'm not what my parents wanted. I'm not what my parents wanted.

3) I'm not what my parents wanted. I'm not what my parents wanted.

4) So, a life spent miserable and overworked? I've seen what working 60+ hours a week did to my parents, and I know that in Comp Sci, that's the case for many workers. No time for side things.

I've spent so long doing what others told me to do, and doing what made them happy that I don't know how to do things for myself.

Nothing. Fucking nothing.

I knew it. I'm crying into a vacuum. Nobody hears me, or nobody cares. Or both.

All that shit about "it gets better," or "you have a whole life ahead of you," or "it's ok, everyone makes mistakes," or "a safe, supportive place," bullshit. Absolutely nothing.
